    Download and Use Google Fonts

    Source: R/use_indiedown_fonts.R
    use_indiedown_gfonts.Rd

    Download a font from Google Fonts with the gfonts package and install it as the main font of an indiedown template package. Documents rendered with the package's output format then use that font. There is nothing to change in the .Rmd.

    Usage

    use_indiedown_gfonts(
  path = ".",
  id = "roboto",
  variants = c("regular", "300italic", "700", "700italic")
)

    Arguments

    path

    Path to the template package, as created by create_indiedown_package(). The fonts are written to inst/indiedown/fonts/ below this path.

    id

    Id of the font, correspond to column id from get_all_fonts.

    variants

    Variants to download, as named by Google Fonts (e.g., "regular", "italic", "700", "700italic"). Exactly four, in the order regular, italic, bold, bold italic. See the section "Where the font files end up".

    Value

    This function is called for its side effects and returns NULL, invisibly.

    Where the font files end up

    The function works on the template package at path, as created by create_indiedown_package(). It writes to the folder inst/indiedown/fonts/ of that package, creating it if necessary, and

    • keeps only .ttf files: everything else in that folder is deleted;

    • renames the downloaded files to regular.ttf, italic.ttf, bold.ttf and bolditalic.ttf, overwriting existing files with these names.

    The new names are assigned by position, not by inspecting the files: the first entry of variants becomes regular.ttf, the second italic.ttf, and so on. variants must therefore have exactly four entries, in the order regular, italic, bold, bold italic. The default uses the light italic ("300italic") of Roboto for the italic slot.

    How the template picks up the fonts

    Because the file names are always the same, the template does not need to know which font was downloaded. The skeleton's inst/indiedown/default.yaml refers to the four files by name:

    mainfont: regular.ttf
mainfontoptions:
- Path=<<indiedown_path>>/fonts/
- BoldFont=bold.ttf
- ItalicFont=italic.ttf
- BoldItalicFont=bolditalic.ttf
- Scale=0.92

    When a document is rendered with the output format of the template package, for example with this YAML header in the .Rmd (where mydown is the name of your package):

    output: mydown::mydown

    the following happens:

    1. The pre_processor of the output format (inst/indiedown/pre_processor.R) calls apply_default_yaml(), which reads default.yaml and replaces <<indiedown_path>> by the location of inst/indiedown in the installed template package (using indiedown_path_tex() from the template package). The settings are handed to pandoc as variables, except for those that are set in the YAML header of the document itself.

    2. The LaTeX template of pandoc turns mainfont and mainfontoptions into a call to the fontspec package, which looks like this (the path is shortened and the line is wrapped here):

      \setmainfont[Path=.../mydown/indiedown/fonts/,BoldFont=bold.ttf,
  ItalicFont=italic.ttf,BoldItalicFont=bolditalic.ttf,Scale=0.92]{regular.ttf}

    3. fontspec needs LuaLaTeX or XeLaTeX. The skeleton's output format uses latex_engine = "lualatex".

    The font is used for all body text: regular text, *emphasis* (italic), **strong** (bold), and both combined (bold italic). The skeleton does not set sansfont or monofont, so code and other text in a sans or monospace family are not affected.

    The font files are read from the installed template package. After running use_indiedown_gfonts(), re-install the package (e.g., with devtools::install()) before rendering a document.

    Using a different font

    • Another Google font: call use_indiedown_gfonts() again with another id and variants. No other file needs to change, because the file names stay the same. The Scale=0.92 entry in default.yaml applies to all fonts; adjust it if the new font looks too large or too small.

    • A font from another source: copy four font files to inst/indiedown/fonts/ and either name them regular.ttf, italic.ttf, bold.ttf and bolditalic.ttf, or adapt mainfont and the BoldFont, ItalicFont and BoldItalicFont entries of mainfontoptions in default.yaml to the file names.

    • A single document: a setting in the YAML header of the .Rmd replaces the corresponding entry of default.yaml as a whole. To change the font for one document, set both mainfont and mainfontoptions there.

    See vignette("walkthrough") for a step-by-step example and vignette("customize") for the other customization points.

    See also

    • create_indiedown_package() to set up the template package.

    • gfonts::get_all_fonts() for the available font IDs, and gfonts::download_font() for the underlying download.

    Examples

    # \donttest{
path <- file.path(tempdir(), "mydown")
create_indiedown_package(path, overwrite = TRUE)
#> ✔ indiedown skeleton set up at /tmp/RtmppIdCmx/mydown
#> ℹ See `vignette("indiedown")` for how to customize the mydown package
# Use Lora, instead of default Roboto
use_indiedown_gfonts(
  path = path,
  id = "lora",
  variants = c("regular", "italic", "700", "700italic")
)
#> ✔ Added lora fonts
# The files always have the same names, whatever the font
list.files(file.path(path, "inst", "indiedown", "fonts"))
#> [1] "bold.ttf"       "bolditalic.ttf" "italic.ttf"     "regular.ttf"   
# }
